memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Obesity-related exertional dyspnea.
Patient reports mild shortness of breath on climbing two flights of stairs, no wheeze or chest pain. Exam: BMI 32 kg/m2, waist circumference 102 cm, blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, lungs clear to auscultation, no cardiac murmurs.
Spirometry: FEV1 3.20 L (92% predicted), FVC 3.80 L (95% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.84; change from baseline not applicable.
Technique checked: no inhaler prescribed.
Smoking status: never smoked (0 pack-years).
Assessment: Dyspnea proportional to obesity; continue lifestyle advice and consider weight‑loss medication.

Obesity-related exertional dyspnea.
Reports reduced breathlessness after walking short distances; still notes fatigue. Exam: BMI 31.2, waist 98 cm, lungs clear.
Spirometry: FEV1 3.28 L (94% predicted), FVC 3.88 L (96% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.85; ΔFEV1 +0.08 L since last visit.
Technique checked: no inhaler prescribed.
Smoking status: never smoked.
Assessment: Mild improvement; continue orlistat, consider uptitrating levothyroxine as TSH slightly elevated.
